## Instructions

Complete this tutorial while reading Sections 5.2 - 5.4 of the [textbook](https://nustat.github.io/intro-stat-data-sci/05-regression.html). Each question allows 3 'free' attempts. After the third attempt a 10% deduction occurs per attempt.

You can click the "View Grade" button as many times as you would like to see your current grade and the number of attempts you are on. Before submitting make sure your grade is as expected.

### Goals

-   Learn how to perform regression for one categorical explanatory variable.
-   Understand the correlation coefficient.
-   Distinguish between correlation and causation.
-   Understand the line of best fit.


## Reading Quiz

```{r Q}
quiz(caption = NULL,
    # Question 1
    question_numeric("Q1) How many European countries are included in the `gapminder2007` dataset?",
           answer(30, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 2
    question_numeric("Q2) What percent of countries in the `gapminder2007` dataset have a life expectancy of less than 71.94?",
           answer(50, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 3
    question_numeric("Q3) How many years higher is the average life expectancy in Europe as compared to Africa? Round to 1 decimal place.",
           answer(22.8, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.1,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 4 (exact match required; hint if only capitalization is wrong)
    question_text("Q4) What is the name of the explanatory variable in `lifeExp_model`? Type the variable name exactly as it appears in the dataset.",
           answer_fn(function(value){
                              if (identical(value, "continent")) {
                                return(mark_as(TRUE))
                                }
                              if (str_to_lower(value) == "continent") {
                                return(mark_as(FALSE,
                                  messages = "Check your capitalization: variable names in R are case-sensitive."))
                                }
                              return(mark_as(FALSE))
                              }),
           trim = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 5 (NEW: baseline group)
    question("Q5) In `lifeExp_model`, which continent is the baseline for comparison?",
           answer("Africa", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Americas"),
           answer("Asia"),
           answer("Europe"),
           answer("Oceania"),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 6 (NEW: why that baseline)
    question("Q6) According to the reading, why did R choose this continent as the baseline?",
           answer("It comes first alphabetically.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It has the lowest mean life expectancy."),
           answer("It has the most countries in the dataset."),
           answer("It has the largest variation in life expectancy."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 7 (NEW: k - 1 offsets)
    question("Q7) If a categorical explanatory variable $x$ has $k$ levels, a regression model returns an intercept and how many additional \"slope\" (offset) coefficients?",
           answer("$k - 1$", correct = TRUE),
           answer("$k$"),
           answer("$k + 1$"),
           answer("$1$"),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 8 (NEW: interpreting an offset)
    question("Q8) In the regression table for `lifeExp_model`, the estimate for `continentAsia` is 15.9. Which is the correct interpretation?",
           answer("On average, countries in Asia had a life expectancy 15.9 years greater than countries in Africa.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("The mean life expectancy of countries in Asia is 15.9 years."),
           answer("On average, countries in Asia had a life expectancy 15.9 years greater than the world average."),
           answer("For every additional country in Asia, life expectancy increases by 15.9 years."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 9
    question_numeric("Q9) When $x$ refers to the country Germany, what is the value of the indicator function $\\mathbb{1}_{\\text{Amer}}(x)$?",
           answer(0, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 10
    question_numeric("Q10) After fitting `lifeExp_model` to the `gapminder2007` dataset, what is the value of $y - \\widehat{y}$ for the country Angola? Round to 3 decimal places.",
           answer(-12.075, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.001,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 11
    question_numeric("Q11) According to `lifeExp_model` fit to the `gapminder2007` dataset, what is the fitted (estimated) life expectancy for the country Bangladesh? Round to 1 decimal place.",
           answer(70.7, correct = TRUE),
           step = 0.1,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 12 (NEW: correlation strength)
    question("Q12) Which of the following correlation coefficients indicates the strongest linear relationship?",
           answer("-0.9", correct = TRUE),
           answer("0.75"),
           answer("0.187"),
           answer("0"),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 13 (NEW: correlation of 0)
    question("Q13) A correlation coefficient of 0 indicates:",
           answer("No relationship: the values of both variables go up/down independently of each other.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("A perfect negative relationship."),
           answer("A weak positive relationship."),
           answer("That one variable causes the other."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 14
    question_text("Q14) What is the confounding variable in the 'sleeping with shoes on' and 'waking up with a headache' example?",
           answer_fn(function(value){
                              if (str_detect(str_to_lower(value),
                                             "alcohol|drink|drunk|intoxic")) {
                                return(mark_as(TRUE))
                                }
                              return(mark_as(FALSE))
                              }),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 15 (NEW: confounding in a causal graph)
    question("Q15) In the causal graph, what makes Z a confounding variable?",
           answer("It affects both the treatment variable X and the outcome variable Y.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It is caused by the treatment variable X."),
           answer("It affects only the outcome variable Y."),
           answer("It is the outcome variable of interest."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 16
    question_numeric("Q16) If all the data points fall perfectly on the regression line, what would be the value of $\\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \\widehat{y}_i)^2$?",
           answer(0, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Question 17 (NEW: least squares)
    question("Q17) Of all possible lines that could be drawn through the points, the regression line is the one that minimizes:",
           answer("The sum of squared residuals", correct = TRUE),
           answer("The sum of the residuals"),
           answer("The number of points that do not fall on the line"),
           answer("The correlation coefficient"),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE)
)
```
